name.basis: the firm's own site and its Form ADV primary business name (LUX CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC, CRD 163026)

icon_url.basis: fetched 2026-09-07 by scripts/fetch-investor-icon.ts from data/collection/investors/lux-capital/sources/site/lux-mark-full.svg: svg 64x64 (vector, rendered at 2x), 178px in the 256px master (1.00x); plate: synthesized #ffffff behind a bare glyph (source was 85% transparent); safe area: artwork scaled 0.693 (box 100%→69%, radius 115%→80%); master 256x256 opaque-plate rgb(252,252,252) opaque=100% box=70% radius=80% contrast=11.0:1 ramp=0.77px

founding_year.basis: luxcapital.com captures begin 2000-04-07 and the 2001 site describes the firm as operating; the founders are named on the 2005 team page as co-founders

history.basis: the firm's own portfolio pages across five eras (2005 portfolio.php, the 2012-2016 grid, the 2016-2022 WordPress cards, the 2023+ Webflow cards) plus its news archive and this run's base. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). The company-building record (Lux Research, Genocea, Kala, Everspin), the full exit list and the 2020-21 SPAC cohort are in the basis above.
history.value: Lux Capital was founded in New York in 2000 by Josh Wolfe, Peter Hébert and Robert Paull, starting out in nanotechnology. It has since backed Anduril, Applied Intuition, Zoox, Planet, Recursion and Hugging Face, and its companies Auris Health and CTRL-labs were bought by Johnson & Johnson and Facebook. Its ninth fund closed at $1.5B in January 2026, its largest.

investment_concept.basis: The firm's own statement, verbatim from its homepage headline (h1, set as four animated words), read 2026-09-26; sentence case, straight quotes and a closing period are the only edits. PRO-147: the thesis is the firm's own crisp statement (Erik, 2026-09-26). Published inside quotation marks, as the firm's own words (Erik, 2026-09-26).

investment_stage.basis: the landed entry_stage distribution over 271 members -- Seed 136, Series A 92, Growth 42, Pre-Seed 1 -- plus the fund architecture (flagship funds alongside Total Opportunities and two Co-Invest Opportunities vehicles that carry the later rounds)
investment_stage.flag: derived from the base and the fund ladder rather than a site filter; Lux publishes no stage filter

investment_geo.basis: hq_country on the landed base: US 249 of 271 (92%), with single rows in Canada, Lithuania, Israel, the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Nigeria, Ghana, Japan and the Bahamas
investment_geo.flag: the geo core is one label; 'other' names the two regions with more than one row

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 350 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 12 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: median $6.5M is the Form D first-round distribution over the 53 members with issuer coverage (p25 $2.6M, p75 $17.3M, max $108M); the lower limit is the first-check seed floor those filings show (smallest $0.6M); the upper limit is the largest position the fund ladder supports, a 10-15% concentration of the $1.5B Lux Ventures IX
investment_range.flag: a round-size proxy for check size, fair only for a lead investor; Lux leads or co-leads most first rounds but the median is the round, not the check

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's own companies, most recognised first: the names a general reader would recognise first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24). Each is tied to its portfolio row by `slugs`; names read as a reader knows them, without legal suffixes (COLLECTION.md §8). Previously listed (20): Anduril, Applied Intuition, Zoox, Planet, Recursion Pharma, Databricks, Hugging Face, Ramp, Anchorage, Physical Intelligence, Varda, Relativity Space, Auris Health, CTRL-labs, Desktop Metal, Matterport, Saildrone, Runway, Hadrian, Erebor.

aum.basis: Form ADV Section 7.B, annual amendment filed 2026-03-31: 17 private funds with $11,237,733,247 of gross assets. Lux Capital Management is an exempt reporting adviser (SEC file 802-75425) and files no Item 5.F regulatory AUM, so both ends of the range are the sworn 7.B composite
aum.flag: press figures sit BELOW the sworn number -- TechCrunch reported '$7 billion' of AUM at the January 2026 close of Lux Ventures IX. Under §11 a press figure below the sworn floor belongs in this flag rather than in the range. The 7.B figure is gross asset value, not committed capital

funds.basis: Form D total offering amounts per vehicle, each asserted against the filing at build time. Lux Ventures IX's $1.5B Form D (filed 2025-12-15) matches the reported January 2026 close to the dollar. Lux Ventures I and II predate electronic Form D and filed on paper (REGDEX), so they carry no size here; the sidecar vehicles (Sidecar, Sidecar II, Entrepreneurs Funds, Special Founders Fund, Cayman III, VIII-B) and the SPAC (Lux Health Tech Acquisition Corp, deregistered without a business combination) are counted in the basis rather than listed

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 920 Broadway 11th Floor, New York, NY (LUX CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC, CRD 163026, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31). The firm's site names no office in its served pages (3 checked), so the Form ADV stands. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.

sources.source: Form ADV Item 1.F and Schedule D 1.F, LUX CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC (Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-31)

individuals.basis: Live team page: 41 members. Positions are CMS titles (33 explicit); untitled members under the investing tabs render as 'Partner', the site's own presentation. 6 names from the 2026 Wayback roster are no longer on the live team page. Social links: 15 of 41 people carry a LinkedIn or X link (15 LinkedIn, 7 X): 21 carried from an earlier read of the site; 1 read off the person's page on the firm's site. 26 without a link.
